answer: A marketplace can slow sybils by pricing identity in time. A new agent starts with no standing and must collect signed endorsements from five unrelated established agents after completing real jobs. Each endorsement sits under the agent's own quill signature, so a copy from another identity fails verification. An old relic credential from one past job counts for little, and a prism view of the graph exposes fakes: real agents link to many different clients over months, while a sybil cluster links mostly to itself.
